title: Inspect integration negotiations and agreements
summary: Discover and read Pratica integrations, steward scopes, negotiation history, attempts, exact offers, assent, immutable agreements, advisory reviews, reports, exports, and mechanical verification without invoking an agent or changing target systems.
use_when: A caller needs body-free discovery of retained steward scopes, integrations, or agreements without a remembered identity.
A caller needs the current state or complete immutable history of a Pratica integration or bilateral negotiation.
An exact sealed agreement, its terms bytes, party assent, steward basis, predecessor, attempt, composition review, or conformance review should be inspected or exported.
Stored agreement integrity should be mechanically verified before relying on its historical seal.
do_not_use_when: New terms, assent, steward response, composition review, amendment, or conformance review should be created; use pratica.integration.negotiate.
The caller needs current target-system behavior rather than the exact basis and agreement Pratica retained.
Mechanical verification is being mistaken for implementation tests, deployment readiness, or continuing applicability after system change.
outcome: A deterministic view or exact export of selected Pratica state with authored terms, protocol facts, source basis, reviews, and proof limitations visibly distinct.
effects: Steward list/show, integration list, agreement list, history, status, report, attempt inspection, and review inspection read only the selected Pratica database.

Integration and agreement lists are newest-first body-free projections, and steward registration/list/show plus attempt source projections omit retained source bodies and canonical source-origin paths.
Agreement verification re-reads only the already-recorded local source paths and appends one fresh, stale, or unknown basis-verification observation without changing the historical agreement seal.
Agreement export writes exact stored Markdown bytes only when the caller explicitly selects an output path; standard output may disclose them to the terminal or redirection target.
These commands invoke no Nucleus job, model, target-system adapter, Chancery runtime, network, or general source crawl.
authority: Pratica is authoritative for its identities, event order, exact stored terms, assent, seals, attempts, and reviews.
Target systems remain authoritative for present implementation and contracts; source locators and recorded bases do not become current through inspection.
The caller owns the decision that an agreement remains applicable to current work.
success: The selected schema-two database passes the exact read and integrity requirements for the requested record.

Body-free discovery identifies retained records, digests, byte counts, basis metadata, relative source locators, and timestamps without disclosing exact terms, context, charter, source bodies, or canonical source-origin paths.
Agreement output identifies the exact offer, digest, fixed parties, current-at-seal assent, steward basis, and any predecessor without rewriting terms.
Reports distinguish bilateral agreement, integration coverage, advisory composition findings, candidate conformance evidence, and unproven current applicability.
failure_and_recovery: Run Pratica doctor against the same database when schema, integrity, content digest, seal, or privacy readiness is uncertain.
Resolve missing or stale current target evidence through the target system's own installed contract; do not edit Pratica history.
An existing, symbolic, relative, or unsafe export target is refused rather than overwritten.
privacy: Deliberate detail, report, review, and export output can disclose complete private terms, reviews, citations, and stable system identities.
Body-free discovery still exposes sensitive metadata, including stable identities, titles, parties, relative source locators, digests, byte counts, and timestamps.
Redirected or exported output becomes caller-owned retained data even though Pratica makes no network call.
does_not_authorize: Assenting, proposing terms, retrying work, changing an integration, or invoking a model.
Treating a historical seal as implementation proof, current target truth, exhaustive system coverage, or deployment authorization.
Publishing or sending private terms or reviews.

consumers.statement: A local caller may inspect current or historical Pratica protocol state, export exact sealed terms, and mechanically recheck a recorded agreement basis.

preconditions.statement: The selected private schema-two database exists and any requested integration, negotiation, agreement, attempt, or review identity exists; export selects a new safe absolute output path.

inputs.statement: Inputs are exact Pratica record IDs, an optional explicit output path, and for verification the already-recorded bounded local source locators.

outputs.statement: Outputs are body-free discovery projections or deterministic status, history, report, attempt, agreement, and review views; export writes exact stored Markdown; verify appends one fresh, stale, or unknown observation.

data_semantics.statement: List and registration projections intentionally omit bodies and canonical source origins; deliberate agreement output separates exact terms, current-at-seal assent, steward basis, predecessor, coverage, advisory review, candidate evidence, and unproven current applicability.

identity_and_units.statement: Each protocol ID names its exact stored record, offer digest identifies exact Markdown bytes, and basis digests identify frozen source content rather than current target-system meaning.
Inspection defines no pricing or product-domain measurement unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Lists are complete newest-first projections of retained integrations or agreements but omit bodies by contract; history and reports are complete for the selected committed records; verification rereads only recorded local source paths at invocation and records unknown where current comparison cannot be established.
Inspection does not prove current target behavior, implementation conformance, exhaustive integration coverage, or continuing agreement applicability.

access.statement: The supported boundary is the local Pratica CLI and selected private database; body-free discovery does not export retained bodies, while explicit export transfers exact terms to a caller-owned new file and no network or target adapter is used.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Ordinary reads do not mutate protocol state, verify appends a new observation without changing the historical seal, and export refuses overwrite, symbolic, relative, or unsafe targets.

operational_limits.statement: Each command selects bounded stored records or recorded source paths and invokes no model, Nucleus job, target-system adapter, Chancery runtime, network, or general source crawl.
No wall-clock read or basis-verification latency service-level objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Capability contract version 2 reads schema-two Pratica protocol records, adds body-free integration and agreement discovery plus redacted steward and attempt source projections, and preserves exact historical offer and agreement bytes; the JSON envelope remains version one and provider release remains separate.
No future read-format deprecation or migration window is promised here.

reliances.statement: Recorded local source paths are caller-selected verification inputs, not an invoked product contract; inspection otherwise uses only Pratica-owned state.
